# `curb_razor_format_code_blocks`

Experimental. Format the C# in @code and @functions blocks of .razor and .cshtml files, and nothing else in them. Read only from a section that names those files.

## Values

| Value | Notes |
|---|---|
| `true` | |
| `false` | |

**Default:** `false`

Experimental. It has to be set in a section whose glob names Razor files, and `[*]`, `[**]` and `[*.*]` do not count, so a catch-all section cannot turn it on by accident:

```ini
[*.{razor,cshtml}]
curb_razor_format_code_blocks = true
```

Without it, Curb never reads a `.razor` or `.cshtml` file. With it, only the C# inside `@code` and `@functions` blocks changes: markup, `@{ }` blocks and expressions are never touched, and a block that holds Razor markup is left as written. See [Razor](../../../workflow/razor.md).

### `curb_razor_format_code_blocks = true`

```ini
curb_razor_format_code_blocks = true
```

::::{tab-set}

:::{tab-item} Before
```html
@page "/counter"

<h1>Counter</h1>
<p role="status">Current count:   @currentCount</p>
<button class="btn" @onclick="IncrementCount">Click me</button>

@code {
  private int currentCount=0;

      private void IncrementCount()
  {
    currentCount+=1;
  }
}
```
:::

:::{tab-item} After
```html
@page "/counter"

<h1>Counter</h1>
<p role="status">Current count:   @currentCount</p>
<button class="btn" @onclick="IncrementCount">Click me</button>

@code {
    private int currentCount = 0;

    private void IncrementCount()
    {
        currentCount += 1;
    }
}
```
:::

::::
